svg.title: Choosing a neuroimaging modality: different objects need different kinds of resolution (spatial, contrast, temporal); radiography, fluoroscopy and CT use X-rays, ultrasound and MRI do not, and each trades its resolution against cost, availability, invasiveness, radiation and scan length; below, what each MRI sequence (T1, T2, FLAIR, DWI, SWI) shows and the order of imaging in a suspected stroke
